title: A cohomology class lifts from a supported perfect object on an affine scheme
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T\subseteq Y$ be closed, and put $U=Y\setminus T$. Let $s\ge0$ be an integer such that $U$ is a union of $s$ affine open subschemes. Let $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category] satisfy $H^j(E)_y=0$ for every $y\in U$ and every integer $-s+1\le j\le0$. For every section $c\in\Gamma(Y,H^0(E))$, there exist a perfect object $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-perfect-complex], a morphism $a:K\to E$, and a section $b\in\Gamma(Y,H^0(K))$ such that $\Gamma(Y,H^0(a))(b)=c$, $H^i(K)=0$ for every $i>0$, and $H^i(K)_y=0$ for every integer $i$ and every $y\in U$. No pseudo-coherence hypothesis on $E$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08E3, lemma-represent-cohomology-class-on-closed, with its proof using the given finite affine cover for the cohomological-dimension bound; the Koszul complex is in nonpositive degrees.

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$. For any $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ let $\beta_L:\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_Y,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(Y,H^0(L))$ be the composite of [lem-pc-derived-structure-sheaf-hom-hypercohomology] with the affine cohomology identification of [lem-sc-qcoh-acyclic-derived-sections-comparison], applied to the identity $Y\to Y$ and the affine open $Y$. The identity is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and its direct image is exact, so its positive derived images vanish. Both identifications are natural in $L$. Let $\psi:\mathcal O_Y\to E$ be the unique morphism with $\beta_E(\psi)=c$.

source.place: Tag 08E3, view the section as a structure-sheaf morphism; Tag 08D4 with N=1 as in Tag 0AVW, affine cohomology identification for the identity morphism

proof.text: Put $R=E|_U$. The stalk hypothesis gives $H^j(R)=0$ for $-s+1\le j\le0$ by [pqf-lem-sheaf-zero-stalks]; restriction to an open is termwise exact. If $s=0$, then $U=\varnothing$, its module category is zero, and $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_U,R)=0$. Otherwise form $L=\tau_{\le0}R\to R\to B=\tau_{\ge1}R\to L[1]$ using [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Its cohomology shows $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_U)^{\le-s}$. The functor $F=\Gamma(U,-)$ commutes with countable products, since products of sheaves are computed on sections. By [lem-sfb-affine-open-finite-cover-cohomology-bound] its higher derived functors on quasi-coherent modules vanish for $p\ge s$. Apply [lem-pc-unbounded-derived-functor-cohomological-bound] with $N=s$ and $b=-s$: $H^i(R\Gamma(U,L))=0$ for $i>-1$. Hence $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_U,L)=0$ by [lem-pc-derived-structure-sheaf-hom-hypercohomology]. Also $\mathcal O_U\in D^{\le0}$ and $B\in D^{\ge1}$, so $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_U,B)=0$ by the orthogonality in [def-weil-t-structure]. Exactness at the middle of $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_U,-)$ for this triangle, [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], now gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_U,R)=0$. In particular $\psi|_U=0$.

source.place: Tag 08E3, first paragraph, using Tag 08D4 and the truncation triangle instead of the bounded-below spectral sequence

proof.text: Choose a finite principal-open presentation $U=\bigcup_{i=1}^{r}D(f_i)$, with $f_i\in A$. Indeed each member of the given finite affine cover is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], hence their union is quasi-compact: restrict an open cover to each member and take the union of its finitely many finite subcovers. The principal opens contained in $U$ cover it by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], so a finite subcover exists. For $U=\varnothing$ take $r=0$. The number $r$ need not equal $s$, and will not enter the cohomological bound. Use the tail objects $I_e$, augmentations $u_e$, full Koszul objects $K_e$, and inclusions $v_e:\mathcal O_Y\to K_e$ of [def-sc-koszul-open-system], indexed here by the positive exponent $e$.

source.place: Tag 08E3 in Situation situation-complex; choose finitely many principal opens without identifying their count with s

proof.text: The morphism $\varphi=\psi\circ u_1:I_1\to E$ restricts to zero, since $\psi|_U=0$. By [lem-sc-koszul-open-hom-restriction-eventually-zero] some later exponent $e\ge1$ makes $I_e\to I_1\xrightarrow{\varphi}E$ zero. The power transitions commute with the augmentations by [lem-sc-affine-perfect-open-represent-cohomology], so this composite is $\psi\circ u_e$. Thus $\psi\circ u_e=0$. (For a zero-based implementation index, the exponent is index plus one.)

source.place: Tag 08E3, second paragraph: the restricted class dies at a finite Koszul stage; Tag 08DD, proposition-represent-cohomology-class-on-open

proof.text: The canonical distinguished triangle of [lem-sc-affine-perfect-open-represent-cohomology] is $I_e\xrightarrow{u_e}\mathcal O_Y\xrightarrow{v_e}K_e\to I_e[1]$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact](i) with target $E$ to the equality $\psi\circ u_e=0$. It gives $a:K_e\to E$ satisfying $a\circ v_e=\psi$.

source.place: Tag 08E3, final sentence: factor the structure morphism through the Koszul cone

proof.text:
Set $K=K_e$. Apply [lem-pc-affine-koszul-geometric-properties] to the tuple $(f_1^e,\ldots,f_r^e)$: $K$ is perfect, and $H^i(K)_y=0$ whenever some $f_j^e
otin\mathfrak p_y$. For $e\ge1$ and a prime $\mathfrak p_y$, $f_j^e
otin\mathfrak p_y$ is equivalent to $f_j
otin\mathfrak p_y$, so this covers every $y\in U$. By [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] the representing cochain complex is zero in positive degrees, so $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>0$. It belongs to $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ because it is the termwise associated sheaf of an $A$-complex, hence in the image of [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence].

source.place: Koszul construction preceding Tag 08E3; nonpositive grading, perfection, and support on the closed complement

proof.text: Define $b=\beta_K(v_e)\in\Gamma(Y,H^0(K))$, using the natural bijection established in step 1 from [lem-pc-derived-structure-sheaf-hom-hypercohomology] and [lem-sc-qcoh-acyclic-derived-sections-comparison]. Naturality for $a$ gives $\Gamma(Y,H^0(a))(b)=\beta_E(a\circ v_e)=\beta_E(\psi)=c$. Together with step 6 this proves every required clause. The argument has used only quasi-coherence of the cohomology of $E$, never pseudo-coherence.

source.place: Tag 08E3, class lies in the image of H^0(Y,K_e) -> H^0(Y,E), with the affine edge identification
